impact: Demonstrated command execution by a hijacked MaxKB agent, outside its sandbox as root in the official container, with an outbound request to an attacker-controlled server. Lasso states, without a specific demonstration, that this design could let one tenant's chat reach another tenant's data and application secrets. Fixed in v2.10.5-lts; no in-the-wild exploitation reported.
mitigations: Upgrade MaxKB to 2.10.5-lts or later, which applies the sandbox to every command the model supplies (Lasso; GitHub advisory).
Use the Docker deployment and confirm the sandbox is actually enabled in the deployment mode; for agents with shell tools, verify isolation is engaged rather than assumed (Lasso).
name: MaxKBypass — prompt injection to command execution outside the MaxKB agent sandbox (CVE-2026-77521)

sources.title: MaxKBypass - From Prompt Injection To Bypassing MaxKB Agent's Sandbox (CVE-2026-77521)
Prompt-injectable agent can lead to command execution (GHSA-f36j-f34j-h3rx)

summary: Lasso Security (researcher Noy Pearl) disclosed MaxKBypass, CVE-2026-77521, in MaxKB, an open-source self-hosted knowledge-base and agent platform from FIT2CLOUD / 1Panel-dev. Attacker-controlled text on a crawled webpage placed in a public knowledge base led the victim's agent to invoke its shell tool during an unrelated question, without the human approval the platform was meant to require; in the official container, commands could run outside the intended sandbox as root. The proof of concept made an outbound request to an attacker-controlled server. The vendor fixed it in v2.10.5-lts and published the advisory, rated critical (CVSS 10.0), on 2026-09-02.
